title: Claude Code
summary: A coding agent with terminal and IDE entry points for repository work.

sources.title: Connect Claude Code to tools via MCP

facts.label: Workflow
facts.value: Terminal, IDE, desktop and web coding agent

facts.label: Privacy / data handling
facts.value: Consumer training settings and commercial terms differ; confirm the account type and opt-in settings.

facts.label: MCP support
facts.value: Claude Code documents local stdio and remote HTTP, SSE and WebSocket MCP server connections; project-scoped servers require workspace trust and approval.

prices.name: Pro
prices.allowance: Shared plan usage limits; not a fixed number of completed tasks

prices.name: Pro — annual commitment
prices.billing: Annual amount paid up front, not a monthly invoice

prices.name: Subscription or API usage
prices.billing: Account-dependent; subscription and API billing are separate
prices.overage: API usage depends on token consumption; do not infer it from a subscription allowance.

sections.heading: Constrain command execution
paragraphs: Start with a repository branch and a specific acceptance test. Inspect proposed commands, file changes and network access before accepting a result. Keep production credentials outside the trial and verify that the task can be rolled back.

sections.heading: Check the account route
paragraphs: Determine whether the session uses a subscription, direct API billing or another supported provider. The applicable spending and data policies follow that account route. A displayed token estimate is not automatically a subscription invoice.

pros.text: The MCP documentation covers local stdio servers and remote HTTP or WebSocket servers.

cons.text: The SSE transport is deprecated; the documentation recommends HTTP when the server supports it.
Project MCP server approvals depend on workspace trust; a cloned repository cannot approve its own servers.

faqs.question: Which MCP transports does Claude Code document?
faqs.answer: It documents local stdio and remote HTTP or WebSocket. SSE is deprecated and HTTP is recommended where available.

faqs.question: Can a cloned project approve its own MCP servers?
faqs.answer: No. Repository project-server approvals are not read from checked-in settings until the workspace is trusted; the cloned repository cannot approve those servers itself.

verdict: Shortlist Claude Code when an explicit repository task and command-based verification fit your workflow. Review command permissions and the account billing route first.
bestFor: Developers comfortable inspecting changes and command results
notFor: Users expecting autonomous changes to be safe without review
migration: Keep build instructions and acceptance tests in the repository. Port tool-specific rules deliberately and review permissions again in the replacement.
